name: Math
topics: Ordinal numbers · Fractions · Bar graph · Word problems

licoes.texto: The value of a digit depends on its place. (Valor posicional.)
pontos: In English, we use a comma to separate thousands: 6,482. In Portuguese we use a period: 6.482.
licoes.fala: The 4 in 6,482 is worth 400 because it is in the hundreds place!

licoes.texto: To round, look at the digit to the right of the place you are rounding to.
pontos: If it is 5 or more, round up. If it is 4 or less, round down.
67 to the nearest ten → 70 (7 is 5 or more).
342 to the nearest hundred → 300 (4 is less than 5).
850 to the nearest hundred → 900 (5 rounds up).
licoes.fala: Five or more, let it soar! Four or less, let it rest!

licoes.texto: Learn the names of the parts:
pontos: 9 × 6 = 54: 9 and 6 are factors; 54 is the product.
20 ÷ 4 = 5: 20 is the dividend, 4 is the divisor, 5 is the quotient.
What is left over is the remainder: 29 ÷ 4 = 7, remainder 1.
licoes.fala: 4 rows of 9 flowers: 4 × 9 = 36 flowers in my garden!

licoes.texto: A fraction is a part of a whole.
pontos: In 3/4: 3 is the numerator (top), 4 is the denominator (bottom).
Equivalent fractions are equal: 1/2 = 2/4 = 4/8.
Same numerator? The smaller denominator is the bigger fraction: 1/2 > 1/4.
licoes.fala: I'd rather have 1/2 of a pizza than 1/8. Bigger slice!

pontos: Right angle = 90°. Acute = smaller than 90°. Obtuse = bigger than 90°. Straight = 180°.
Parallel lines never meet. Perpendicular lines meet at a right angle.
Triangle (3 sides), quadrilateral (4), pentagon (5), hexagon (6), octagon (8).
licoes.fala: Ângulo reto is “right angle”. Same idea, new words!

licoes.texto: Perimeter is the distance around a shape. Area is the space inside it.
pontos: Perimeter: add all the sides. Rectangle 5 cm × 3 cm → 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 cm.
Area of a rectangle: length × width → 5 × 3 = 15 cm² (square centimeters).
licoes.fala: Perimeter is the fence around the garden. Area is the grass inside!

pontos: o'clock: 3:00. Quarter past: 15 minutes after (9:15).
Half past: 30 minutes after (3:30).
Quarter to: 15 minutes before the next hour (8:45 = quarter to 9).
licoes.fala: Half past three means three thirty. Snack time!

questions.q: How do you write the ordinal number for 3?
questions.fb: Os três primeiros são irregulares: 1st first, 2nd second, 3rd third. Depois disso quase todos ganham “-th”.

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 5?
questions.fb: Five → fifth (o “ve” vira “f”). O mesmo acontece com twelve → twelfth.

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 9?
questions.fb: Nine → ninth: o “e” cai antes do “-th”. É uma das poucas exceções, vale decorar.

questions.q: My birthday is on the 21st of May. How do you say it?
questions.fb: Em números compostos, só a última parte vira ordinal: twenty-first, thirty-second, forty-third.

questions.q: The family lives on the 12th floor. How do you say it?
questions.fb: Twelve → twelfth. Os ordinais são muito usados para andares, datas e posições numa fila.

questions.q: What fraction of this shape is shaded if 1 of 4 equal parts is coloured?
questions.fb: O número de baixo diz em quantas partes dividimos (4) e o de cima quantas pintamos (1): one quarter.

questions.q: How do you read the fraction 3/4 in English?
questions.fb: 3/4 = three quarters (ou three fourths). 1/2 = one half e 1/3 = one third.

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 1/2?
questions.fb: Frações equivalentes representam a mesma quantidade: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8. Dividir em mais partes e pegar mais delas dá no mesmo.

questions.q: A builder used 1/2 of 48 bricks. How many bricks did he use?
questions.fb: Metade de 48 = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 bricks.

questions.q: There are 20 windows in a building and 3/4 of them are open. How many are open?
questions.fb: Primeiro ache 1/4: 20 ÷ 4 = 5. Depois multiplique por 3: 5 × 3 = 15 windows.

questions.q: Which fraction is bigger: 1/3 or 1/6?
questions.fb: Quanto mais partes, menor cada pedaço. Dividir em 3 dá pedaços maiores do que dividir em 6.

questions.q: In a bar graph, what does the tallest bar show?
questions.fb: Quanto mais alta a barra, maior a quantidade. A barra mais baixa mostra a menor.

questions.q: A graph shows favourite house materials: brick 12, wood 8, straw 5. How many children answered in total?
questions.fb: Basta somar todas as barras: 12 + 8 + 5 = 25 children.

questions.q: Using the same graph (brick 12, wood 8, straw 5), how many more children chose brick than straw?
questions.fb: “How many more” pede subtração: 12 − 5 = 7 children.

questions.q: Why does a bar graph need a title and labels?
opts: Only to make it look nice
So the reader knows what the data is about
questions.fb: Sem título e sem os nomes dos eixos, as barras viram números soltos. Eles dizem o que está sendo contado e em que unidade.

questions.q: Each wall needs 250 bricks. How many bricks for 4 walls?
questions.fb: É multiplicação: 250 × 4 = 1.000 bricks.

questions.q: A bag of cement costs R$ 35. How much do 6 bags cost?
questions.fb: 35 × 6 = 210. Fazendo por partes: 30 × 6 = 180 e 5 × 6 = 30, somando R$ 210.

questions.q: You have R$ 500 to build a wall. You spend R$ 320. How much is left?
questions.fb: 500 − 320 = 180. Controlar quanto sobra é exatamente o que se faz num orçamento (budget).

questions.q: 144 tiles will cover 12 equal floors. How many tiles per floor?
questions.fb: Dividir igualmente: 144 ÷ 12 = 12 tiles. Conferindo: 12 × 12 = 144 ✓

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 2?
questions.fb: 1st first · 2nd second · 3rd third — os três irregulares que é preciso decorar.

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 8?
questions.fb: Eight → eighth: o “t” do final se junta ao “-th”, ficando só um t.

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 20?
questions.fb: Twenty → twentieth: o “y” vira “ie” antes do -th. O mesmo em thirty → thirtieth.

questions.q: Which is the ordinal number for 30?
questions.fb: Thirtieth (30º). Cuidado para não confundir com thirteenth, que é 13º!

questions.q: In a race, the runner who arrives right after the third one is in which place?
questions.fb: Depois do third (3º) vem o fourth (4º). Note: four perde nada, só ganha -th.

questions.q: How do you say the date 1 May?
questions.fb: Datas em inglês usam ordinais: the first of May, the second of June, the third of July.

questions.q: How do you read the fraction 1/3 in English?
questions.fb: One third. Em inglês, os denominadores usam os números ordinais: third, fourth, fifth…

questions.q: How do you read 2/5?
questions.fb: Two fifths — com s no final, porque é mais de uma parte.

questions.q: A pizza is cut into 8 equal slices and 5 are eaten. What fraction was eaten?
questions.fb: ⚠️ A pergunta é sobre o que foi comido: 5 de 8 → 5/8. Se contar o que sobrou dá 3/8 — outra pergunta!

questions.q: Which fraction is equivalent to 2/4?
questions.fb: 2/4 = 1/2. Dividindo em cima e embaixo por 2, chegamos à fração mais simples.

questions.q: There are 24 bricks and 1/4 of them are red. How many are red?
questions.fb: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 bricks.

questions.q: Which is more: 3/4 or 1/2 of the same cake?
questions.fb: 1/2 = 2/4, e 3/4 é mais que 2/4. Então 3/4 é o pedaço maior.

questions.q: In a bar graph, what does the vertical axis usually show?
opts: The quantity or number of items
questions.fb: O eixo vertical (de pé) traz os números; o horizontal traz as categorias.

questions.q: A graph shows houses built: 2021 → 15, 2022 → 20, 2023 → 12. In which year were fewest houses built?
questions.fb: 2023, com 12 casas — a menor barra. “Fewest” quer dizer o menor número.

questions.q: Using the same graph (15, 20 and 12), how many houses were built altogether?
questions.fb: 15 + 20 + 12 = 47 houses. “Altogether” pede a soma de tudo.

questions.q: If each square on the graph stands for 2 houses, how many houses does a bar of 6 squares show?
questions.fb: 6 × 2 = 12 houses. Sempre confira a escala antes de ler o gráfico!

questions.q: A builder has 96 tiles and uses 48. How many are left?
questions.fb: 96 − 48 = 48 tiles left.

questions.q: A window costs £45. How much do 3 windows cost?
There are 156 bricks to share equally between 4 walls. How many per wall?
questions.fb: 156 ÷ 4 = 39 bricks. Conferindo: 4 × 39 = 156 ✓

questions.q: A house has 3 floors with 4 rooms on each floor. How many rooms in total?
What does the word “altogether” tell you to do?
questions.fb: Altogether e in total pedem soma. Já “how many more” e “left” pedem subtração.

questions.q: Put the ordinal numbers in order
questions.fb: ⚠️ Watch the spelling: it is fifth, not "fiveth".

questions.q: Match each number to its ordinal
questions.fb: 1, 2 and 3 are the irregular ones. From 4 on, most just add -th.

questions.q: Put the fractions in order, from smallest to biggest
questions.fb: ⚠️ Careful: with the same numerator, the bigger the denominator, the SMALLER the fraction. 1/4 is smaller than 1/3.
